newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EURO-MPs to back fund for EU film industry.
newsitem.headline: EURO-MPs to back fund for EU film industry.

text.p: Euro-MPs are expected on October 21 to back the European film industry's call for a European Union guarantee fund to help it survive competition from Hollywood productions.
"We need to support the production and distribution of European cinema and television films," an official from the European Parliament's culture committee told Reuters on Tuesday.

"Banks tend to give loans to safe investments, especially U.S. productions, which are easier to distribute than European ones. The aim of the fund is to encourage banks to lend to productions which have (distribution) problems," he explained.

Euro-MPs are due to adopt a report by French Union for Europe deputy Armelle Guinebertiere which backs a European Commission proposal for a 200-million-Ecu fund, to which the EU and the private sector would each contribute 90 million Ecus, with the European Investment Bank providing the remaining 20 million.
The proposal -- COM(95)546 -- needs the unanimous support of all 15 EU member states to become a reality.
Germany, the Netherlands and Britain have opposed the plan.

But Philippe Kern of the European Film Companies Alliance said the Hague and London may soften their approach in the light of a new study from the Commission which says the fund could be financially viable for 17 years.
The parliament could also use its budgetary powers to try to force ministers' hands, the cultural committee official said.

EU finance ministers recently rejected a Commission proposal to begin contributing to the fund in 1997. Euro-MPs could reinsert an as-yet undefined allocation in the 1997 budget when they vote on it in December.
"We are not talking about spending Community money. This is a guarantee. It would only be spent if the producer was unable to reimburse the loan," the official pointed out. REUTER
